question: does a SPIKING dopamine nucleus decide the Go/NoGo effective-circuit mode from reward/context?
sources: Schultz Science 275:1593-1599 (1997) / J Neurophysiol 80 (1998) signed DA RPE
read-out: Randi et al. Nature 623:406-414 (2023) perturb-and-measure (board #63)
base capability: board #64 neuromod reconfiguration GO
substrate: nav basal ganglia (build_bg_brain_regions flagship A+E); DA nucleus = snc (IZH2007_DOPAMINE)
mechanism: dopamine_mode: from_region_firing_signed on [snc] -> concentration; excitability_drive D1(+)/D2(-); reward/context = afferent current to snc. No set_concentration.
label: spiking DA nucleus SELF-DRIVES the Go/NoGo effective-circuit mode from reward/context

preconditions.name: determinism: byte-identical F re-run @ fixed seed
SELF-DRIVEN: SNc fires more in appetitive than aversive (gap>0, min over seeds)
SELF-DRIVEN: DA level appetitive > aversive (gap>0, min over seeds)
SAME WIRING: max|W_app - W_ave| == 0 (anatomy identical across contexts)
RECONFIG: spearman(F_app, F_ave) < 0.9 (below the same-pattern 1.0), max over seeds
DOUBLE DISSOCIATION: >=1 edge opened ONLY in appetitive/Go, every seed (min)
DOUBLE DISSOCIATION: >=1 edge opened ONLY in aversive/NoGo, every seed (min)
ROBUST: spearman(F_app,F_ave) EXCL snc row/col still < 0.9 (genuine D1/D2 reconfig), max over seeds
DA-NUCLEUS-DRIVEN: reconfiguration collapses when the SNc nucleus is silenced
SNC-LESION: silenced nucleus -> F_app == F_ave byte-for-byte (max|dF|==0)
